purpose: R3b-2A resurrection witnesses for remote-seat-mail-transport/v1. Each row removes one load-bearing behaviour and names the witness that must turn red without it. The ten contract vectors passed on their first run, which proves nothing on its own; these rows are what shows them failing for their own named reasons.
prefix_allocation: Whole token RM allocated to R3b-2A by the coordinator in the approved contract after refusing Q, which the live R3c1 candidate c851d63c already owns (Q01-Q12). L is R3c2-D's; PL and Z remain active claims. Re-inventoried immediately before this manifest's first commit: 200 manifests across every author root under C:\fixtures plus canonical dev at be1c33c2 -- zero RM rows.
guard_disclosure: run.py carries TWO guards by ruling. The allocation guard refuses any row whose id is not a whole-token RM[0-9]+; the selection guard refuses a --prefix that is not exactly RM, rather than silently matching nothing and exiting zero. The manifest also fails closed when unreadable, malformed, empty, missing a required key, or carrying a duplicate id.
isolation: Every mutation is applied inside its own disposable git worktree at the exact candidate commit. No mutant is written into the calling worktree, so there is no restore step that could leave a stale build behind.
scope_note: R3b-2A owns the transport half only. Rows for local admission, ack-debt and checkpoint advancement (R3b-2B), the coalesced wake bit, reconnect scheduling and the Live declaration (R3b-2C), and end-to-end crash cuts (R3b-2I) are deliberately ABSENT rather than approximated here.
uncovered_by_design: The admission packet's resurrection list includes mutants this lane cannot carry because their subject does not exist in this crate: advancing a checkpoint before ack-debt settlement, erasing debt after a lost response, inferring progress from local consumed rows, clearing a signal received during catch-up, allowing a second catch-up owner, replacing the capacity-one signal with an unbounded queue, and reconnecting forever. Each belongs to B or C and is recorded here rather than silently dropped.
j2_note: The admission packet's 'allow a second catch-up owner' mutant is not merely out of scope, it is SUPERSEDED. Ruling J2 removed leases and fences, so a second opener is legitimate; RM15 witnesses the replacement law instead -- a takeover that fails to name whom it displaced.

mutations.law: Advisory B: the diagnostic bound settles to the SMALLER side
mutations.note: min -> max. A provider that can carry only 64 diagnostic bytes is handed 4,096. Attributed to the diagnostic arm alone: the body, page and aggregate arms are untouched, so RM10/RM11 stay green and only the diagnostic witnesses fire.

mutations.law: Advisory B: a post-open diagnostic uses the SETTLED bound, not the ceiling
mutations.note: The R1 defect itself: `max_diagnostic_bytes` is advertised, mandatory, negotiated and then ignored in favour of the hardcoded ceiling. This is the mutant that would have been GREEN against the previous candidate, because the previous candidate had no other behaviour.

mutations.law: Advisory B: truncation lands on a UTF-8 boundary at the NEGOTIATED bound
mutations.note: Stops walking down to a character boundary. `String::truncate` panics rather than producing invalid UTF-8, so the witness fires on the panic — the law is still 'never split a character', and the language enforces the consequence.

mutations.law: B2: settling consults the provider's own measurement, not a constant
mutations.note: Replaces a measured provider value with the local ceiling. This is the shape B2 removed the unreachable `LimitError` in favour of: the profile is complete by type, so the only way to break it is to stop READING it.

mutations.law: Advisory D / J8: a dismiss carries the pair ITS BINDING authenticated
mutations.note: Resurrects the caller-authored pair: the request stops reading the binding and asserts a fixed pair instead. Two bindings over DIFFERENT project pairs then produce requests that agree, which is exactly the authority confusion J8 forbids.

mutations.law: Advisory C: an exact repeat is EVERY coordinate, not just the ack id
mutations.note: Collapses identity onto one coordinate, so a DIFFERENT message or digest reconciles as an exact retry — a lost response would then silently accept a different fact under the original receipt. ack.rs carried zero RM rows at R1 despite owning this law.

mutations.law: Advisory C: an exact retry is not a first record
mutations.note: Makes a retry claim it created the record. The delivery count then inflates once per lost response, which is the duplicate-fact defect the ExactRetry variant exists to prevent.
